title: Broad Mite on Sweet Pepper - Barbados

Header: Broad Mite on Sweet Pepper - Barbados

Prevention: Plant crops in a clean field, free from host crop debris.

Avoid growing near any host plants, e.g. apple, avocado, cantaloupe, castor, chilli, citrus, coffee, cotton, eggplant, grapes, guava, jute, papaya, passionfruit, pear, potato, sesame, string or pole beans, mango, tea and tomato.
Rotate sweet pepper with non-host species (from outside the same family).
Control whitefly populations as the mites can be transported by whiteflies.
Monitoring: The pest is insidious and not usually noticed until damage is excessive.
Regular inspection of the crop is required.
Inspect the plants every two to three days.
Carefully inspect the meristematic / apical parts especially flower buds for distortion and fruits for brown russetting.
Remove affected leaves and buds for laboratory diagnosis.
To sample plants place in zip lock bags and freeze to kill pests, then have a lab inspect them.
Direct Control: Insecticidal soap (fatty acids) at a rate of 2 tea spoons per gallon.
Remove all affected plants from the field.
Experiments have shown that immersion in hot water (110 degrees
Fahrenheit) for 15 mins will kill the mites.
Care is required not to damage the plants.
